- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.50) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for downward correction.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts, especially after 1–2 bullish days; apply smoothing filter to avoid overshoots.
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often fails to correct; reduce subsequent forecast by 3–8% to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., -0.50, -1.00), model tends to lag in recognizing trend reversal; adjust forecast downward 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early period (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late period (last 5–7 days); apply asymmetric weighting: reduce early forecast, increase late forecast if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
